reasoning_traces.think:
The study contrasts two contest success functions (CSFs): the Tullock ratio form EWP = rs^α/(rs^α + ra^α) and the logistic difference form EWP = 1/(1 + e^{α(ra - rs)}). The former treats runs scored and allowed as competing ratios, while the latter models the differential directly through a logistic link. Both are derived from the broader class of contest success functions that map performance differentials to win probabilities. The simulation-based validation on 1000 MLB seasons shows that the logistic form outperforms the ratio form in terms of R², RMSE, and AIC. This suggests that the marginal value of runs scored relative to runs allowed is best modeled as a logistic function of their difference rather than as a ratio. The implications for GSI involve using the logistic form to calibrate team strength priors, while for GSE, it enables more accurate game-state transitions by modeling how run differentials evolve over time. The failure mode of the ratio form lies in its assumption of symmetric competition dynamics, which may misrepresent asymmetric scoring environments.
